newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria to invest $1.27 bln to boost cotton exports.
newsitem.headline: Syria to invest $1.27 bln to boost cotton exports.

text.p: Syria's public and private sectors are investing about $1.27 billion to build new cotton spinning mills to boost exports to world markets, industry minister Ahmed Nezamuldin said on Thursday.
He told Reuters in an interview the projects, to be completed during the next three years, would allow Syria to spin most of its output of ginned cotton.

The minister said annual production is around 650,000 tonnes of raw cotton yielding about 225,000 tonnes of ginned cotton. Production is expected to reach a record 700,000 tonnes of raw cotton this year.
Syria's spinning mills currently have a capacity to treat 80,000 tonnes of ginned cotton while the rest is exported.

"The new projects will allow us to gain a lot of hard currency in exports as the difference between the ginned and spinned cotton could in some grades be as high as $7,000 per tonne," Nezamuldin said.
He said the government, as part of its encouragement to the private sector, had allowed private investors to engage in the spinning industry which previously was entirely in the public sector.

He said 107 spinning and textile projects costing around 28.39 billion Syrian pounds ($675 million) had already been approved and some of these projects with total capacity of 52,000 tonnes of ginned cotton would start production within two years.
He said the government was now investing $600 million to build four spinning mills and to expand existing ones. The projects would raise capacity to 146,000 tonnes from 80,000 tonnes.
The projects include one spinning mill in Edleb, some 320 km north of Damascus, being constructed by Spain's Alfamatex at a cost of $134 million.
The project with a capacity of 15,000 tonnes will start test production early next year, the minister said.

A second spinning mill has started test production in Latakia on the Mediterranean, some 350 km northwest of Damascus. Builty by Germany's Hamburg-based Peco Trading company at a cost of about $122 million, it has a capacity of 15,000 tonnes.

A third project involves expanding the Latakia mill to produce an additional 12,000 tonnes of spinned cotton, at a cost of $100 million. Peco Trading won the contract and construction will start soon and is expected to be completed within 24 months.
China's Textile Industry Foreign Economic Cooperation Co won the right to build the fourth spinning mill which will have a capacity of 24,000 tonnes per year and cost $190 million.
Construction of the mill at Jableh, on the Mediterranean some 300 km northwest of Damascus will start soon, the minister said.

He said the government was also spending $50 million to renovate some existing mills to maintain the levels of current production, and planned to double capacity of a wool spinning plant to 1,200 tonnes a year from 600 tonnes at a cost of $12 million.
He said the textile industry is second only to oil in economic importance. It is the country's largest employer, with 270,000 employees, one third of Syria's industrial workforce.
"Textiles are the oldest industry in Syria...The oldest loom in the world was made in Damascus," the minister said.
